system.name: ExoPlane
system.one_liner: an operating system that augments on-rack switch resources with external devices via a packet-pinning model

components.name: Network Operator
components.role: provides device information, cross-app requirements, and objective functions as input

components.name: Developer(s)
components.role: provides P4 programs plus app-specific requirements and state synchronization logic as input

components.name: P4 programs
components.role: developer-supplied P4 program code fed into the ExoPlane planner

components.name: ExoPlane planner (§5)
components.role: profiles P4 programs, computes optimal resource allocation, and merges P4 programs into one program

components.name: Profiling P4 programs
components.role: planner sub-step that profiles resource use of the input P4 programs

components.name: Optimal resource allocation
components.role: planner sub-step that allocates switch and external-device resources across applications

components.name: Merging P4 programs
components.role: planner sub-step that merges multiple applications' P4 programs into one program

components.name: Merged P4 program
components.role: planner's output program deployed onto the on-rack resource augmentation architecture

components.name: On-rack resource augmentation arch.
components.role: the switch plus external-device hardware that executes application processing

components.name: Prog. Switch
components.role: programmable switch that runs the merged program and can hand packets to external devices

components.name: External devices
components.role: auxiliary devices attached to the rack that process packets pinned to them

components.name: ExoPlane runtime environment (§4)
components.role: places workloads on devices, manages app state, and handles load balancing and external-device failures at runtime

components.name: Workload placement
components.role: runtime sub-function that places applications and flows on switch or external devices

components.name: Load balancing and fault handling
components.role: runtime sub-function that balances load and handles external-device failures

content.key_idea: ExoPlane splits control into a long-term planner that merges and allocates developer P4 programs from operator/developer inputs, and a short-term runtime environment that places and rebalances workloads on the switch and external devices.
content.reading_order: Top-down: Network Operator and Developer(s) inputs (green) feed the ExoPlane planner (blue, long-term), which outputs a merged P4 program to the on-rack hardware, managed at runtime by the ExoPlane runtime environment (yellow, short-term).

Green boxes represent inputs and yellow and blue boxes indicate key modules.

summary: This figure gives an overview of ExoPlane, an operating system for augmenting on-rack switch resources with external devices under a packet-pinning model. Green boxes show the inputs: a Network Operator supplies device information, cross-app requirements, and objective functions, while Developer(s) supply P4 programs, app-specific requirements, and state synchronization logic. These feed the blue ExoPlane planner (§5), a long-term-planning module that profiles P4 programs, computes optimal resource allocation, and merges the programs into one Merged P4 program deployed on the on-rack resource augmentation architecture (the programmable switch and external devices). The yellow ExoPlane runtime environment (§4) is the short-term-management module that handles workload placement and load balancing and fault handling at runtime. A small color legend at the left explicitly maps green/yellow/blue to system input, long-term planning, and short-term management.
summary_zh: 该图展示ExoPlane系统概览：绿色为系统输入（网络运营商与开发者提供的信息和P4程序），蓝色ExoPlane规划器负责长期资源分配并合并P4程序，黄色ExoPlane运行时环境负责工作负载放置与故障处理。
